issues.t: Water pump leaking coolant or whining
issues.sym: Pink or reddish coolant drips under the passenger side of the engine, a sweet smell, the coolant level keeps dropping, or a grinding or squealing noise from the belt area.
issues.why: The water pump seal on this 1.8L engine (the same engine used in the Corolla and Matrix) wears out early. Toyota issued a service bulletin for coolant leaks and noise from the pump. It is the most-reported repair for the xD.
issues.next: Check the coolant level when the engine is cold and top up if low. If the temperature gauge climbs, stop driving to avoid overheating. Have the pump replaced, and replace the drive belt at the same time.

issues.t: Engine failure or blown head gasket at high mileage
issues.sym: White smoke from the exhaust, coolant loss with no visible leak, overheating, loss of power, or a loud knock followed by the engine quitting. Most reports come at around 100,000 to 115,000 miles.
issues.why: Engine problems are the most-reported category for the 2008 xD. Owners report blown head gaskets, compression loss and, in some cases, a failed connecting rod. Overheating from a leaking water pump or low oil can lead to this kind of damage.
issues.next: Stop driving if the engine overheats, knocks or smokes heavily. Have a shop do a compression or leak-down test to find out whether the head gasket or the whole engine is damaged before deciding on a repair.

issues.t: Oil leak from the timing chain cover
issues.sym: Oil seeping down the passenger side of the engine, oil spots under the car, or a burning oil smell after driving.
issues.why: The sealant along the timing chain cover on this engine can weep oil as the car ages. The oil pressure switch nearby can also leak and is a cheaper fix, so it should be ruled out first.
issues.next: Keep an eye on the oil level. Ask a shop to confirm exactly where the leak comes from, since the oil pressure switch is much cheaper than resealing the timing cover. A small weep can be watched; a steady drip should be fixed.

issues.t: Engine burning oil
issues.sym: The oil level drops between changes, sometimes with blue smoke from the exhaust or an oil-fouled spark plug.
issues.why: Toyota issued a service bulletin for oil consumption on this 1.8L engine. Owners report a dealer engine computer update as the fix.
issues.next: Check the dipstick every few fill-ups and top up as needed. Ask a Toyota dealer whether your car has had the oil-consumption bulletin done.

issues.t: Brief rattle or knock at cold start
issues.sym: A short knocking or rattling sound for a second or two right after starting a cold engine, then it goes away.
issues.why: The camshaft timing gear (the part that adjusts valve timing) can rattle briefly before oil pressure builds up. Toyota issued a service bulletin for this noise and replaces the gear.
issues.next: This is not an emergency, but have it checked so a dealer can confirm it is the timing gear and not something more serious. Keep up with oil changes using the correct 0W-20 oil.

issues.t: Long cranking, no start or misfire codes
issues.sym: The engine cranks for a long time before starting or won't start at all, sometimes with the check engine light on for misfires (P0300-P0304) or cam timing (P0015).
issues.why: Toyota issued a service bulletin for no-start, extended cranking and these codes on early xDs. Owners report carbon buildup and an engine computer update as the fix.
issues.next: Have the codes read and ask a Toyota dealer whether the bulletin applies. Also check the battery and its terminals, since a weak battery can cause similar slow starts.

issues.t: Misfire from a failed ignition coil
issues.sym: The engine shakes or runs rough, feels down on power, and the check engine light comes on or flashes, often with a code from P0301 to P0304.
issues.why: Each cylinder has its own ignition coil, and they can fail with age and heat. Owners report replacing one or more coils, often at 100,000 miles or more.
issues.next: If the check engine light flashes, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off. Have the codes read; the coil is usually quick to swap, and old spark plugs should be replaced at the same time.

issues.t: Alternator stops charging
issues.sym: The battery warning light comes on while driving, lights dim, the battery keeps going flat, or the car dies and won't restart. Steering may get heavy if the voltage drops far enough.
issues.why: The alternator is one of the most-replaced parts on the xD, often failing somewhere between 40,000 and 140,000 miles.
issues.next: If the battery light comes on, head to a shop while the car still runs, and turn off accessories you don't need. Have the charging system tested before buying a new battery.

issues.t: ABS, VSC and brake lights on from a rear wheel speed sensor
issues.sym: The ABS, stability control (VSC) and brake warning lights come on together, sometimes coming and going. Anti-lock braking may not work, especially in snow.
issues.why: The rear wheel speed sensors and their wiring on the 2008 xD fail often, sometimes after corrosion or freezing. ABS and VSC warning lights are among the most-reported brake complaints for this year.
issues.next: Normal braking still works, but ABS may not, so leave more stopping room, especially on slick roads. Have the ABS code read (often C0210 or similar) to find which sensor or wiring has failed.

issues.t: Clunk from the front suspension over bumps
issues.sym: A clunk or knock from the front of the car when driving over bumps or rough pavement.
issues.why: Toyota issued service bulletins for front suspension clunk on 2008-2012 xDs, and extended warranty coverage on a front lower control arm bolt.
issues.next: Have the front suspension inspected so any loose bolt or worn part is found. Ask a Toyota dealer about the bulletin and whether any coverage still applies.

issues.t: Noise or vibration from an engine mount when accelerating
issues.sym: A groan, thump or vibration felt in the cabin when you accelerate or shift gears.
issues.why: Toyota issued a service bulletin for abnormal noise and vibration from the side engine mount when accelerating. Noise or vibration on acceleration is one of the problems RepairPal lists most for the xD.
issues.next: Have the engine mounts inspected. A worn mount is not dangerous right away but can let the engine move more and strain other parts.

issues.t: Water on the passenger floor from a blocked A/C drain
issues.sym: Wet carpet or a puddle on the front passenger floor, usually after running the air conditioning.
issues.why: The tube that drains condensation from the A/C can clog with debris or insect nests, so water backs up into the cabin. Toyota issued bulletins for this on 2008-2012 xDs, and again for insect nests.
issues.next: Have the A/C drain tube cleared, and dry the carpet so it doesn't get moldy. The fix is usually quick and cheap.

issues.t: Musty smell from the air vents
issues.sym: A musty or sour smell from the vents, mostly when the A/C or fan first comes on.
issues.why: Moisture left on the A/C evaporator lets mold and bacteria grow. Toyota issued a bulletin on HVAC odors and how to reduce them.
issues.next: Replace the cabin air filter and ask a shop about an evaporator cleaning. Turning off the A/C a few minutes before you park, while leaving the fan on, helps the system dry out.

issues.t: Clear coat cracking or peeling
issues.sym: The shiny top layer of paint turns cloudy, cracks or flakes off, usually on the roof, hood and other sun-facing panels.
issues.why: Clear coat failure is the top body complaint for the 2009 xD and shows up on 2008 cars too. Owners report Toyota declining to cover it.
issues.next: This is cosmetic, but bare paint will eventually rust. Get a body shop quote to refinish the worst panels, and keep the car waxed or parked out of the sun.

issues.t: Driver's power window switch can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: The driver's window switch feels sticky or works on and off, gets hot, or gives off a burning smell or smoke.
issues.why: The grease on the switch contacts was applied unevenly at the factory, so the switch can short, overheat, melt and possibly start a fire. Toyota issued two recalls (12V-491 for 2008-2009 and 15V-689 for 2009-2010).
issues.next: If you smell burning or the switch gets hot, stop using it and have the car checked. Look up your VIN for open recalls; the dealer inspects, regreases or replaces the switch for free.

issues.t: Front seat may not lock in place (recall)
issues.sym: The driver's or front passenger seat slides or won't stay locked after you adjust it.
issues.why: Springs in the seat rails can break, so the seat may not latch and could move in a crash. Recall 14V-169 covers xDs built from April 2007 to May 2010.
issues.next: If a seat won't lock firmly, don't use that seat until it is fixed. Check your VIN for open recalls; the dealer inspects and replaces the seat rail for free.

issues.t: Hard brake pedal in extreme cold (recall)
issues.sym: In very cold weather the brake pedal feels hard and the car takes longer to stop.
issues.why: Moisture from the engine's crankcase ventilation could freeze in the port that feeds vacuum to the brake booster, reducing power assist. Recall 09V-338 covers 2008-2009 xDs in cold-weather states.
issues.next: If the pedal feels unusually hard in the cold, brake earlier and gently and have the car checked. Look up your VIN; the dealer installs a redesigned intake connector for free.

issues.t: Load capacity label missing or wrong (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom. The door-jamb label showing how much weight the car can carry may be missing or show the wrong numbers, mostly on cars with dealer-added accessories.
issues.why: Labels on some cars didn't meet federal requirements, which could lead an owner to overload the car. Recalls 10V-035 and 10V-036 replace the labels.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls; the label is replaced for free. Until then, don't load the car beyond what the owner's manual allows.

issues.t: Starter clicks but engine won't crank
issues.sym: You turn the key and hear a single click, or nothing, and the engine doesn't turn over, even though the lights work.
issues.why: The starter motor wears out with age and high mileage. A weak battery or corroded terminals can cause the same symptom and should be checked first.
issues.next: Check that the battery terminals are clean and tight and have the battery tested. If the battery is good, the starter is the likely cause.

issues.t: Wheel bearing hum
issues.sym: A humming or growling noise that gets louder with speed and may change when you turn. Vibration in corners at high mileage.
issues.why: Wheel bearings wear out over time. They are among the most-reported repairs on the xD, and on the rear they come as a hub assembly with the ABS sensor.
issues.next: Have it checked soon. A badly worn bearing can overheat or let the wheel wobble, so don't ignore a growl that keeps getting louder.

issues.t: Manual transmission clutch slipping or wearing out
issues.sym: On manual cars, the engine revs climb without the car speeding up, the clutch engages high on the pedal, or there's a burning smell after hills.
issues.why: Clutch wear is one of the most-reported problems on the xD, with some owners needing a clutch as early as 55,000 miles.
issues.next: Avoid resting your foot on the clutch and hard launches. If it slips, have it replaced before it leaves you stranded, and have the flywheel checked at the same time.

issues.t: Clicking from a worn CV axle
issues.sym: A clicking or popping noise when turning sharply, or grease thrown around the inside of a front wheel from a torn rubber boot.
issues.why: The front axle joints and their rubber boots wear with age. A torn boot lets dirt in and grease out, and the joint then wears quickly.
issues.next: Have the axles and boots inspected. Catching a torn boot early can save the joint; a clicking joint usually means the axle should be replaced.

issues.t: Check engine light from the fuel vapor (EVAP) canister
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with an evaporative emissions code, and it comes back after the gas cap is replaced.
issues.why: Owners report water getting into the charcoal canister that stores fuel vapors, or the canister failing, which causes vapor-system leak codes.
issues.next: Make sure the gas cap clicks tight first. If the light returns, have a smoke test done to find the leak. It's not urgent, but the car may fail an emissions test.

issues.t: Rear brakes or parking brake sticking
issues.sym: Grinding or scraping from the rear, the car pulling or dragging, a hot wheel, or a parking brake that stays stuck on.
issues.why: Rear brake parts can rust and seize if they aren't cleaned and lubricated, especially in winter climates. Owners report frozen calipers and parking brakes.
issues.next: Have the rear brakes cleaned and checked at least once a year. If a wheel is very hot or smells burnt after driving, get it looked at before driving further.

issues.t: Radio or audio display goes blank or stops working
issues.sym: The radio or the display goes blank, a connected iPhone won't show on the screen, or the head unit stops working.
issues.why: Owners report replacing the factory radio, and Toyota issued bulletins for a blank display with some iPhones and for audio software updates.
issues.next: Try a software update at a dealer before paying for a new radio. If the unit is dead, a replacement or aftermarket unit is the usual fix.
